workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The concurrently proposed Codex named-pools collector emits 7-day titles that this classifier misses
leads.consequence: If both changes land, default and GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark 10080-minute windows get titles 'Weekly limit' and 'GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark Weekly limit', respectively. limitWindow trusts explicit titles, isWeeklyWindow requires Weekly to be the final word, and both valid 7-day meters render without the six dividers. This PR's tests still pass on a clean combined Panel. PR #7543 is currently CONFLICTING against the base branch, not stacked with this one; this is a conditional integration defect, not a claim that the two PRs have already merged. Consider classifying a typed duration/period independently of presentation title or recognizing the producer's precise title contract, and assert its two 7-day cases in integration tests.

leads.summary: The new test passes even if the dividers are disabled
leads.consequence: The test evals the classifier and checks its wiring text, but never asserts that Meter instantiates six delegates, places them at sevenths, or paints an opaque color. A plausible accidental edit replacing 'model: meter.weekly ? 6 : 0' with 'model: 0' removes every divider while all 17 panel test assertions continue to pass. Add an assertion on the repeater model/geometry and alpha, or preferably a QML component-level render test. This is distinct from whether the current revision's tests pass (they do).

leads.summary: Opaque dividers become colored bars rather than literal background cuts on fully transparent popup themes
leads.consequence: When a user sets [popups] background-alpha = 0, the popup card transmits the content beneath it, but the six dividers still paint the popup's raw RGB at alpha 1. Thus they are six opaque stripes over whatever is behind the transparent popup, not transparent holes that show the same underlying pixels as the card. With partial transparency they similarly need not match the visibly composited card. This improves visibility over an alpha-0 separator but qualifies the PR description's 'cuts ... in any theme' claim. A genuinely theme-matched cut requires either clipping/masking the meter to reveal the already rendered card or accepting that opaque cuts are a chosen accent, not the background itself.

leads.summary: Concurrent popup-gradient theme PR makes all six separators the first stop's opaque color, including on other-color regions
leads.consequence: If #13120 lands, KeyboardPanel renders the configured multi-stop gradient but Color.popups.background remains the first-stop flat color by that PR's explicit contract. The weekly meter draws all six opaque cuts in that first-stop RGB regardless of their x position, so for e.g. the documented blue-to-purple 90deg background, dividers against other-colored parts cannot match the card, even at popup alpha 1. The panel file does not overlap this PR, so the dependency changes without a textual conflict. Consider clipping to reveal the rendered background or a gradient-aware cut before both merge; a screenshot in a gradient-themed nested desktop would confirm visual salience.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator (coord/pr13120.diff: color-only consumers use first stop; PR open, mergeable_state dirty); conditional on a conflicting unmerged PR; applies equally to the pre-change colour, so not a property of this commit

leads.summary: Concurrent pace tick PR conflicts in the same Meter child block
leads.consequence: #11892 adds a pace tick at exactly the Meter position this PR fills with its Repeater. The two heads diverge (not stacked), and combining with their own PR merge base produces a conflict in that child block. Applying #11892's Panel diff to this head rejects hunk 5 even though #11892 is individually MERGEABLE against quattro. A maintainer must preserve both the six dividers and the pace tick and decide stacking order: a divider painted above the tick can obscure the marker at seventh boundaries. No combined code exists yet, so no test was claimed to pass on it.

leads.summary: Concurrent estimated-window title PR can remove dividers from estimated weekly records
leads.location: shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml:145-146 and open PR #11022 windowTitle() at :89-106
leads.consequence: The independently proposed #11022 preserves a collector's '(est.)' marker by making a 'Weekly (7-day, est.)' label into the title 'Weekly (est.)'. For an untitled record of that documented shape, this PR's end-anchored Weekly check then produces a plain meter despite its 7-day label. No shipped default collector currently emits '(est.)' limit labels, so this is conditional on an external/estimated collector (the panel accepts third-party record files) and #11022 merging; it is not a defect demonstrated with stock Claude/Codex. Either preserve a typed period independent of display suffix or jointly account for this precise marker in the classifier and test.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1.4); conditional on #11022 plus an external estimated-limit collector; no stock producer emits it

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Follow-up** to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12527#issuecomment-5827767666) of `1db18001`, checked at head `d788a82e` ("Pick the weekly limit meter by its title").

**Verified:** all three earlier points are resolved, and no regressions were found in the checked scope. One unmeasured edge case of title matching is noted below.

| Earlier point | Now |
|---|---|
| "Weekly" decided by time until reset | Resolved |
| Dividers blend with a translucent popup background | Resolved |
| Test passed with or without the change | Resolved |

### Weekly classification: resolved

**Verified:** `isWeeklyWindow` ([`Panel.qml:145`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/d788a82ee394cd8df46a859b604c0b3b8ab9d433/shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml#L145)) tests the trimmed title against `/\bweekly$/i` and no longer reads the reset clock. Run through the current Claude and Codex collectors:

```text
Input                              title             dividers   before
Claude seven_day, 2 h to reset     Weekly            6          none
Claude seven_day, no resets_at     Weekly            6          none
Codex 10080 min, resetsAt null     Weekly            6          none
Claude weekly_scoped               <model> Weekly    6          6 (> 6 h left)
Claude five_hour / Codex 300 min   Session           none       none
"<model> Monthly" (if sent)        <model> Monthly   none       6 (> 6 h left)
Codex 43200 min                    Session           none       6 (> 6 h left)
```

Every known 7-day input from the current collectors is classified weekly, and every known non-7-day input is not. Qt's own QML engine gives the same results as Node for the helper. The updated PR description now matches the collector, which builds model-scoped titles as `name + " " + "Weekly"`.

**Note on title matching:** the check now depends on the producer's title. A Codex window reported with a null or zero `windowDurationMins` is labelled "Limit" by [`limit_window`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/d788a82ee394cd8df46a859b604c0b3b8ab9d433/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex#L498-L512) and gets no dividers even if it is weekly. The old rule drew dividers on it while more than 6 h remained, but it did the same for any window with that much time left, since such a window's length is unknown. This is a limit of title matching rather than a regression. The Codex protocol types the duration as nullable, but no current input with a null duration was observed, and how often it occurs was not measured. Open PR #7543 would title Codex weekly windows "Weekly limit", which the anchored pattern also skips.

### Divider colour: resolved

**Verified:** `root.alpha(root.surface, 1)` uses the existing `alpha(c, a)` helper ([`Panel.qml:50`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/d788a82ee394cd8df46a859b604c0b3b8ab9d433/shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml#L50)), so the dividers are the popup background colour at full opacity. On in-tree themes (all at `popups.background-alpha` 1.0) they are unchanged. Contrast arithmetic, not a render, over black, white and grey wallpaper for four themes:

```text
Divider against the fill      popup alpha 1    alpha 0.5       alpha 0
before                        7.06 to 21       2.68 to 5.28    1.0 (invisible)
now                           7.06 to 21       7.06 to 21      7.06 to 21
```

On a translucent popup the dividers now appear as solid ticks in the popup colour on a see-through card, rather than as see-through cuts. The PR description's "read as cuts ... in any theme" is slightly broader than that.

### Tests: resolved

**Verified:** `test/shell.d/agents-panel-test.sh`, including the new block, passes at the head (17 ok, 11 from the new block) and with the PR's two files laid over the current `quattro` tip. It fails on the merge base and on `1db18001` at "agents panel exposes its weekly-window helper". Reverting the helper to the old reset rule, or binding `weekly: false`, also fails it.

**Optional test improvement:** a mutant with `Repeater { model: 0 }` (no dividers drawn) still passes all 17 assertions. A regex on `model: meter.weekly ? 6 : 0`, next to the existing binding check, would catch the dividers being dropped.

**Related open PR:** #11892 ("Mark the pace on agent limit meters") adds a pace tick at the same place in `component Meter`. A three-way merge of the two `Panel.qml` versions gives one conflict there, and both are pace guides on the same meter.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** follow-up at head `d788a82e`. Source inspection of the panel, the Claude, Codex and Fireworks usage collectors, theme colour handling and related open PRs. The two test files that read `Panel.qml`, test mutants, a collector title matrix, a headless QML evaluation of the helper and contrast arithmetic were run in an isolated sandbox. Nothing was rendered, so divider appearance and fractional scaling are unverified. Real provider payloads were not queried, and the full test suite was not run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
